title: PR #27: Free shipping on orders of $50 or more

overview.whole_task: We're giving [[shipping-quote|free shipping on US orders of $50 or more]], and the cart now shows [[free-shipping-banner|a progress bar of how close you are]].

footprint.label: Shop web app
footprint.change: A new shipping rule (gift cards, coupons, bulky items, orders abroad) that the cart total and a new progress banner both use.

ship_facts.deploy_order: Just a normal web app deploy.

overview.before_state: Every order paid a flat $5.99 for shipping, no matter how big it was.
overview.after_state: US orders of $50 or more ship free, and the cart shows a progress bar toward it.

visuals.caption: Here's the end result: a $62 cart gets the green banner and pays $0.00 for shipping.

concepts.what_it_is: The one answer the shop gives about shipping for a cart, in one of three shapes.
how_it_works: **`nothing_to_ship`:** the cart is empty or only has gift cards.
**`international`:** the shopper is outside the US, so it's a flat $19.99 plus bulky fees.
**`domestic`:** a US price plus `leftForFreeCents`, how much more is needed for free shipping.
concepts.pr_impact: New in this PR. The cart total and the banner both read the same quote, so they can't disagree.

concepts.what_it_is: The part of the cart that is compared with $50: physical items only, after the coupon.
how_it_works: **Gift cards:** left out, because they're emailed and would let a $50 gift card unlock free shipping.
**Coupon:** taken off first, so $55 with 10% off ($49.50) doesn't qualify.
concepts.pr_impact: New in this PR and used only by `shippingQuote()`.

concepts.what_it_is: The shop's existing helper that works out how much a percent-off coupon takes off, in cents.
how_it_works: **Rounding:** rounds down to a whole cent, so the shop never gives more than the coupon says.
concepts.pr_impact: Not changed. The $50 check reuses it so it sees the same discount the customer sees.

concepts.what_it_is: An optional per-item delivery fee for big things like furniture and lamps.
how_it_works: **Per unit:** two lamps pay the fee twice.
**Missing:** most items don't have one, which counts as $0.
concepts.pr_impact: Not changed. Free shipping removes the standard $5.99 but keeps these fees.

concepts.what_it_is: The function that adds up the subtotal, discount, shipping and total that the cart page shows.
how_it_works: **Callers:** the cart page, and any other page that shows an order total.
concepts.pr_impact: Gets a third `country` argument (default US) and now also returns the shipping quote.

concepts.what_it_is: A message at the top of the cart about free shipping, with a progress bar.
how_it_works: **Under $50:** yellow, says how much more to add, and fills a bar.
**$50 or more:** green, and mentions bulky fees if there are any.
concepts.pr_impact: New in this PR, placed right under the "Your cart" heading.

concepts.what_it_is: An existing hook that returns the two-letter country of the shopper's saved address.
concepts.pr_impact: Not changed. The cart page now passes its answer into the shipping quote.

chapters.title: The free-shipping rule
chapters.summary: One new file decides [[eligible-subtotal|what counts toward $50]] and [[shipping-quote|what shipping costs]], with tests for every tricky case.

chapters.title: Using it in the cart
chapters.summary: [[cart-totals|The cart total]] switches to the new rule, and the cart page gets [[free-shipping-banner|a progress banner]].

steps.title: What counts toward the $50
steps.explanation: First we decide [[eligible-subtotal|which part of the cart counts toward free shipping]], and the three answers [[shipping-quote|a shipping quote]] can give.

rows: Yes, after the coupon comes off
Yes, but their own delivery fee is still charged

diff_highlights.title: One of three answers
diff_highlights.explanation: A quote is one of three shapes, and only the domestic one has `leftForFreeCents`, so TypeScript forces the total and the banner to handle every case instead of guessing.

diff_highlights.title: Gift cards out, coupon off
diff_highlights.explanation: Gift cards are dropped before adding up, so a $50 gift card can't unlock free shipping on a $5 mug, and [[coupon-discount|the coupon comes off]] before we compare with $50.

steps.title: Pricing the shipping
steps.explanation: Next, `shippingQuote()` turns the cart into one answer: nothing to ship, a flat rate abroad, or a US price with how much is left to $50.

diff_highlights.title: Gift cards only? Nothing to ship
diff_highlights.explanation: If every item is a gift card there's nothing to put in a box, so we return a separate answer instead of pretending it's a free US order.

diff_highlights.title: Bulky fees always apply
diff_highlights.explanation: Each [[bulky-fee|bulky item adds its own delivery fee]] per unit, and that fee is added on top later even when the $50 makes standard shipping free.

diff_highlights.title: Abroad: flat rate, no free shipping
diff_highlights.explanation: Outside the US free shipping doesn't exist, so we return early with the flat $19.99 rate plus bulky fees and never work out how much is left.

diff_highlights.title: The actual $50 check
diff_highlights.explanation: The amount left never goes below zero, and a cart at or over $50 pays $0 base shipping but still keeps any bulky fees.

diff_highlights.title: The sneaky coupon test
diff_highlights.explanation: A $55 jacket with 10% off costs $49.50, so this cart still pays $5.99 and is exactly 50 cents short of free shipping.

visuals.source_label: Cart page with a bulky item
visuals.caption: A $62.50 cart ships free, but the floor lamp's $15.00 delivery fee is still charged.

steps.title: The cart total uses the quote
steps.explanation: Now `cartTotals()` asks the new rule for shipping instead of always adding $5.99.

diff_highlights.title: Country defaults to US
diff_highlights.explanation: Other pages that call `cartTotals()` with two arguments keep compiling, but they also quietly get US shipping prices until they pass a country.

diff_highlights.title: Turning the quote into a number
diff_highlights.explanation: Only `nothing_to_ship` has no `costCents`, so it becomes $0 here, and the whole quote is returned too so the banner reads the same answer as the total.

callouts.text: Heads up: this only changes the total the web app shows. Check that the payment server charges the same way, or a $60 order could show free shipping and still be charged $5.99.

steps.title: The progress banner on the cart page
steps.explanation: Last, the cart page [[shipping-country|reads the shopper's country]] and shows [[free-shipping-banner|a banner with a progress bar]] toward free shipping.

points.text: It says how much more to add and fills a bar.
It turns green and says you've got free shipping.

diff_highlights.title: Only US orders see it
diff_highlights.explanation: Free shipping only exists for US orders, so the banner stays hidden both for gift-card-only carts and for shoppers abroad.

diff_highlights.title: Why `> 0` and not just `&&`
diff_highlights.explanation: Writing `quote.costCents && …` would print a stray 0 on the page when there's no bulky fee, so `> 0` turns it into true or false first.

diff_highlights.title: Round down, never up
diff_highlights.explanation: Rounding down keeps the bar from showing a full 100% at $49.99, which would look like free shipping while the shopper is still a cent short.

diff_highlights.title: A bar screen readers understand
diff_highlights.explanation: The bar is a real progressbar with a label and 0 to 100 values, so screen readers announce the progress instead of skipping a plain colored box.

visuals.caption: Before: a $37.50 cart just pays $5.99, with no hint that free shipping exists.

visuals.label: After
